item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Ukrainian drones have intensified attacks on St Petersburg, striking oil facilities, a refinery, a bridge and data centers, while a separate strike hit a Russian oil terminal. President Trump has waived several Russia sanctions, prompting Zelenskyy to accuse him of rewarding Putin, and Lithuania has foiled an arson attack on Starlink equipment suspected to involve Russia. Zelenskyy says Russia seeks a total blackout of Ukraine's energy grid as winter approaches, and Ukraine continues to rely heavily on Starlink communications. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Settlers in the West Bank are intensifying attacks during the olive harvest, torching cars and trees, wounding farmers, and assaulting European diplomats, a US photographer and a French mayor. In Gaza, families are reuniting after a ceasefire while a 7‑year-old girl was killed by Israeli fire and UNICEF reports 340 children killed despite the ceasefire. The EU has condemned the settler attacks on diplomats and demanded accountability. The Board of Peace is urging Israel to admit Gaza technocrats and an international force. The conflict caused 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Iran is providing targeting and intelligence to the Houthis for attacks on Saudi Arabia, and Egypt has pledged to give Saudi Arabia necessary support in the Houthi conflict. item.description:

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:

Iran and Iraq foreign ministers discussed regional security, including the Hormuz Strait, Palestine and Yemen conflicts, and the Kurdistan Regional Government warned that a coalition exit could enable an ISIS resurgence. item.description:

The militia also reports that Eritrean forces have suffered losses in the fighting. The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate the conflict. Hospitals in Tigray have resumed operations as supplies arrive, and the conflict caused 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen have intensified attacks on security forces, with ISWAP claiming a strike that killed 21 soldiers and militiamen at an army base, while unknown gunmen assaulted police stations in Plateau, Abia, and Borno, killing multiple officers. Bandits have also used landmines, killing eight soldiers on a Borno highway and another eight near the Cameroon border, and they abducted an air traffic controller in Sokoto, who remains captive after 52 days. President Tinubu approved security equipment to protect trains from bandits, indicating a response to the rising bandit threat. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

In Haryana, two individuals were held for allegedly attacking a bus bound for Srinagar, prompting condemnation from Kashmir leaders and the Mirwaiz, who called for strict legal action. Manipur’s Kamjong district saw renewed violence with a Kuki civilian killed, fifteen houses torched in a suspected militant attack, and a gunfire incident that injured two civilians, including a village chief. item.title: The Sahel insurgency: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen killed an immigration officer and wounded another in Niger State, while bandits killed one and abducted three in Niger. Rival jihadist groups JNIM and IS-linked factions clashed in northwestern Nigeria and in Burkina Faso, where IS claimed over 400 JNIM fighters were killed. The United States added Nigeria to its blacklist for recruiting child soldiers, and Mali expanded its reserve force by 2,400 recruits, including 800 women. The conflict produced 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Hezbollah explosives seized from two Lebanese trucks have led Lebanon's prime minister and security forces to promise a thorough investigation while Israeli artillery and air strikes continue against Hezbollah positions in southern Lebanon, causing civilian casualties. In northern Israel a Hezbollah submunition exploded in a teenager's backpack, killing Elazar Yair Wilensky and wounding dozens, prompting an IDF probe and possible hike restrictions. Qatar has pledged funding for reconstruction in southern Lebanon, announced a massive solar plant project, and its foreign minister called for Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon. The UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Cabo Delgado, Mozambique: the situation
item.description:
Mozambique's army is now reported to be losing a crucial counter-insurgency battle in Cabo Delgado, indicating a setback for security forces against the insurgents. The government continues its December deadline for civilians to surrender illegal firearms and has recently killed another member of the Anamola group in the province. Forces linked to Erik Prince suffered a battlefield loss in Congo, with a former UFC fighter among the wounded, showing the conflict's regional spillover. The insurgency caused 151 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Libya: the situation
item.description:
Libyan armed forces have executed 31 people after unfair military trials, breaking a 15‑year moratorium, while rights groups report eastern authorities carrying out executions and 50 detainees face imminent execution. Heavy rainfall in Tripoli caused at least three deaths in one incident and two deaths in separate incidents, adding to flood-related casualties. The European Union has expanded migration cooperation with eastern Libya, and China has called for an end to Libya’s political deadlock. A football match between Morocco and Libya will be broadcast on beIN SPORTS as part of the 2026 Futsal AFCON. There were two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
